name: Luke Nosek

summary.text: Luke Nosek earned a B.S. in computer engineering from the University of Illinois in 1996, where he co-founded SponsorNet New Media with Max Levchin and Scott Banister, then worked as an evangelist at Netscape. University of Illinois profiles describe him as a 1998 co-founder of PayPal (Confinity) and its vice president of marketing (and strategy). In 2005 he co-founded Founders Fund with Peter Thiel and Ken Howery. He became a SpaceX director, and in 2017 he left Founders Fund to launch Gigafund. No public record was found of outside funding for his ventures before 1999, or of ties to finance, government or intelligence before PayPal.

openQuestions: Nosek's exact Confinity start date, title and equity are not in PayPal's S-1; a primary record (Confinity filings, Soni's The Founders) is needed.
Secondary accounts say Nosek pointed Levchin to Thiel's 1998 Stanford talk; not verified from a primary source in this session.
A secondary history (scaruffi.com) calls Nosek a Stanford Review editor; this conflicts with his University of Illinois degree and was not verified.
No record found of SponsorNet's investors, revenue or outcome.
The University of Illinois describes Founders Fund's SpaceX investment as '$20' (apparently $20 million, year not stated); exact amount and date not verified.
